provisional_line: These figures are under a methodology review and will be revised.
survivorship_line: Our data provider's free tier carries no delisted companies, so this test only ever saw names that survived to today. Every return below is flattered by that.
notes: Historical earnings dates are projected backwards on a quarterly cadence from the next known date. The earnings filter is therefore approximate.

metrics.label: CAGR
metrics.help: The single yearly rate that would turn the starting capital into the ending capital over this period.

metrics.label: Best year (2026)
metrics.help: The calendar year with the largest gain, and what it was.

metrics.label: Worst year (2024)
metrics.help: The calendar year with the largest loss, and what it was.

metrics.label: Worst fall
metrics.help: The deepest fall from a peak in the account to the low that followed it, before a new peak was made.

metrics.label: Won
metrics.help: Share of closed trades that made money after costs.

metrics.label: Average gain
metrics.help: Average return of the trades that made money.

metrics.label: Average loss
metrics.help: Average return of the trades that lost money.

metrics.label: Mean
metrics.help: Average return across every closed trade, winners and losers together.

metrics.label: Median
metrics.help: The middle trade: half did better, half did worse.

metrics.label: Trades passed up
metrics.help: Signals that qualified on the day but were not taken because the maximum number of positions was already held.

metrics.label: Period in a strong market
metrics.help: Share of sessions where the benchmark closed above its 200-day average.

summary: Over 2.0 years, $100,000 became $106,248 on 16 trades, holding at most 5 at a time and cutting a loser at 8%. 29 more signals qualified and were passed up because the book was already full. 58% of the period was a strong market by this test's own definition — the benchmark above its 200-day average.

benchmark.help: Holding the benchmark from the first session of the period to the last.
